The row's approach prose is right; road.status and road.driveNote wrongly call the FR 51 stretch gravel.

results.fact: Whether the 17-20 mile hike-in is done in one day
results.evidence: A 2025 climbing trip report did the 18+ mile Chewuch approach to Upper Cathedral Lake in one sunrise-to-sundown day, which contradicts 'Nobody does this in a day', but it used a different trail. A regional hiking guide recommends 3-4+ days round trip for Upper Cathedral Lakes, and another trip report split the Chewuch approach over two days. No two sources establish either 'most parties' or 'nobody' for the Andrews Creek hike-in, so no patch.

results.correct_value: The approach trails are well graded with no bushwhacking; stretches of Andrews Creek through the burn can be overgrown.
results.evidence: A regional guide describes the Cathedral Lakes trails as in good shape and well graded; a 2025 climbing trip report says the Chewuch trail is well maintained with no bushwhacking or scrambling. A 2022 hiker report (seen only in search summary) says Andrews Creek was clear of deadfall but overgrown in the burn zones, so the approach card's overgrown tread holds. The pro_tip overclaims ('every trip report', 'well-maintained') and cites reports as a source; reworded to the supported, non-conflicting fact.

patches.find: every trip report calls the approach mellow, well-maintained trail with no bushwhacking.
patches.replace: the approach trails are well graded with no bushwhacking, though stretches through the burn can be overgrown.
